findings.issue: No test infrastructure whatsoever: no test script, no runner (vitest/playwright) in devDependencies, zero test files in app/ for 974 LOC of script.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest and cover the pure helpers in api.ts (humanize, dexNumber, latestFlavorText, idFromUrl, toSpeciesCards) plus filter/sort logic — all are DOM-free or easily testable via jsdom.

findings.issue: Latent bug no test would miss: the 150 ms search debounce closure survives navigation; if the user types then clicks a card within the window, apply() runs updateUrl(new URL('/', location.href)) and replaceState's the Pokémon page URL into '/?q=…', corrupting history and back navigation.
findings.suggestion: Cancel the debounce on teardown (e.g., abort when the element is disconnected or on render token change), and add a regression test that types then immediately navigates.

findings.issue: toSpeciesCards implements the trickiest business rules (drop IDs > 10000, map Pokémon→species, dedup, sort by dex) with no coverage; swapping the dedup set for the wrong key or dropping the sort would silently reorder 'Learned by'/'Pokémon' lists.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with fixture refs including deoxys-normal, an alternate form, and a duplicate species ID.

findings.issue: readFilters/filtersUrl URL round-trip is untested: page=0/NaN/negative handling, default-parameter omission, and filter-change resetting page to 1 (app/src/pages/home.ts:117).
findings.suggestion: Property-style tests asserting filtersUrl(readFilters(url)) normalizes any URL, plus a test that changing a filter on page 3 resets to page 1.

findings.issue: Moves-table sort: missing-values-last in BOTH directions, aria-sort on exactly one header, and second-click flip are all untested; a refactor of the sign multiplication could put nulls first when descending.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator and test with rows containing null power/accuracy, ascending and descending.

findings.issue: The hand-rolled server's SPA fallback and ROUTES allowlist are untested; a regex regression (e.g. forgetting /? on /types/) returns a hard 404 for deep links, and the traversal guard at app/server.mjs:43 is security-adjacent.
findings.suggestion: A few supertest/node:test cases for deep-link 200, non-route 404, and ../ rejection would be cheap and high-value.

findings.issue: Game/method ordering logic — sort by version-group order with Infinity fallback, METHOD_ORDER ranking then alphabetical tiebreak — is untested; adding a new learn method or a group missing from /version-group would reorder tables wrongly.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the ordering with a fixture set including an unknown method name.

findings.issue: latestFlavorText relies on 'last en entry in API order' plus whitespace collapsing; a refactor to .find() would pass the acceptance suite only if the fixture happens to differ, and no app test would catch it.
findings.suggestion: Trivial one-line unit tests for latestFlavorText and humanize ('mr-mime' → 'Mr Mime').

findings.issue: The renderToken race guard is correct-looking but untested; any refactor of the async render path risks reintroducing out-of-order page replacement.
findings.suggestion: An integration test with a stubbed slow fetch asserting the later navigation wins would pin this down.

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own — no runner, no script, zero files — despite ~970 lines of exactly the kind of pure, DOM-free logic (text helpers, species mapping, comparators, URL serialization) that is cheap to unit-test in a Vite project. Once the provided Playwright acceptance suite stops being the guard, regressions in filtering, pagination, sorting, and the custom static server would ship silently. The only positive static check is tsc --noEmit in the build script; the untested debounce path in home.ts already hides a real history-corruption bug.
